results.title: India Bat Against Pakistan in Asian Games Cricket Final; Teenager Kumkum Mohod Wins Archery Gold
results.description: India are batting at 58 for the loss of two wickets after four overs in the men's cricket gold medal match against Pakistan at the Asian Games , hours after 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod won India's first individual women's recurve gold. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was caught behind the wicket, walking back at 15 (9), while Sanju Samson was dismissed after scoring just two runs. Abhishekh Sharma is batting at 38 (12) and has been joined by skipper Shreyas Iyer at the crease for India, who were put in to bat after India won the toss and chose to bat first. The final is the first men's cricket meeting between India and Pakistan at the Asian Games. The captains did not shake hands at the toss, according to Cricinfo. India kept the same XI that beat Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the semifinal. Besides the openers, the batting has Sanju Samson, Iyer, Ishan Kishan, Tilak Varma and Shivam Dube, with Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Ravi Bishnoi and Jasprit Bumrah as the bowling options. Pakistan, led by Sahibzada Farhan, also named an unchanged side from their semifinal win. Farhan is the batter to watch; he has two half-centuries in four T20I innings against India, averaging 38.75, and his nine sixes against them are the most by a Pakistan batter in T20 internationals. Samson, dismissed for seven in the semifinal, has a T20I strike rate below 100 against only Pakistan, although he has faced them just twice. Earlier in the day, Sri Lanka took the bronze medal by beating Bangladesh by 63 runs. Tharindu Ratnayake made 65 off 32 balls and took two wickets. Historic Archery Gold On the archery range, Kumkum Mohod beat South Korea's Oh Yejin 6-5 in a shoot-off after the final finished level at 5-5. Oh shot an 8 and Mohod answered with a 10. The teenager trailed 2-0 and 3-1, then levelled with a perfect 30 in the third set. After losing the fourth set, she forced the shoot-off with three 10s in the fifth. She had earlier beaten South Korea's world and Olympic champion Kang Chaeyoung 6-4 in the quarterfinal and China's Zhu Jingyi 6-2 in the semifinal. Her gold makes her the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve medal at the Asian Games. It also adds to India's only previous individual recurve medal, Tarundeep Rai's silver at the 2010 Guangzhou Games. On Friday, Mohod won women's recurve team gold with Ankita Bhakat and Kirti Sharma, beating South Korea 5-3, which was India's first Asian Games medal in that event. She also took mixed team silver with Dhiraj Bommadevara, after India lost 3-5 to China. India's medal tally stands at 77, with 17 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze, at the time of writing.
